description: We are a team passionate about space exploration, software development, and creative problem-solving. Our goal is to develop an interactive Space Mission Design Game that allows users to create, customize, and manage their own space missions. Players will face real-world challenges involving spacecraft design, resource management, orbital mechanics, and mission planning. We aim to combine education and entertainment to create an engaging experience that inspires curiosity about space exploration
summary:
We developed a video game in which you play as an astronaut stranded on Mars. For some strange reason, you are also the person responsible for organizing all kinds of space missions, meaning that you must plan and coordinate your own rescue mission.

Planning and organizing this space mission is no easy task. It involves managing a budget, purchasing supplies, designing components, calculating trajectories, managing time and personnel, and responding to unexpected events.

All these elements are presented in a simple and easy-to-understand way. The purpose of our video game is to demonstrate everything involved in planning a space mission while making the experience accessible and engaging. Since these missions involve numerous variables and complex scientific concepts, planning one can seem overwhelming, stressful, and intimidating.

Through a project like this, young people around the world will be able to visualize themselves participating in a space mission and dare to dream of becoming part of space exploration, removing the intimidating aspects without sacrificing the mission's realism and scientific accuracy.
details:
We developed a video game in which you play as an astronaut stranded on Mars. For some strange reason, you are also the person responsible for organizing all kinds of space missions, meaning that you must plan and coordinate your own rescue mission.

From your screen, you will have access to a monitor with four main menus. The first one is the shopping menu, where you can order and purchase materials that you will use to design and build the spacecraft's components.

The second one is the maintenance menu. Unfortunate events can occur both on Mars and on Earth, delaying or affecting our progress. These events include power outages, communication failures, and sandstorms, among others. Their appearance affects the pace of the game and limits access to several options necessary for mission planning. That is why, in the maintenance window, you can assign yourself or a group of workers to repair or mitigate these problems.

The third window is the Design Menu, where you can design the components needed to build your rocket using the materials you have previously acquired.

Finally, in the Rocket Launch Menu, you can perform launch simulations to practice and calculate the rocket's trajectory, as well as carry out the mission's final launch.

As we can see, the video game incorporates many variables and different aspects of real-life space missions. However, we have made sure to simplify these processes so that they are easy to understand and enjoyable for young people.

Through this project, we hope that players will be able to understand and enjoy the process of planning a space mission. Many young people dream of participating in these kinds of missions, but that dream is often held back by the fear of how complex and difficult they might be. Our goal is to help those dreams move forward, allowing young people to see space missions from a different perspective and giving them the confidence to pursue their ambitions.

The video game was developed using the Godot game engine. We also used Figma and GitHub to design the interface and organize our work, respectively. Additionally, Claude and Gemini were used to assist with the development of the game's code.

The creativity behind our project lies in the small details. Although our main objective is to simplify complex concepts, we also strive to include as many variables as possible to make the experience more realistic, without sacrificing simplicity or making the game overly simplistic.

One example of this can be found in the launch platform, which works through trajectory calculations using the mouse. Its movement determines the rocket's speed and trajectory. Originally, simply reaching the surface of Mars was enough for the mission to be considered successful. However, we decided to introduce an additional layer of realism: if the rocket reaches Mars at an excessively high speed, it crashes into the Martian surface, resulting in mission failure.

This is an example of how we incorporate greater realism into the game while keeping the mechanics simple, accessible, and enjoyable for players.
